hint: A limit asks where the values are heading. For a smooth, unbroken rule like this one, you can simply substitute.

hints.text: A limit asks where the values are heading. For a smooth, unbroken rule like this one, you can simply substitute.
Put $x = 2$ into the rule $3x + 1$, which gives $3(2) + 1$. Work that out.
The value is $6 + 1 = 7$, so the expression approaches $7$.

explanation: The rule $3x + 1$ is a straight line, so it has no holes and no breaks near $x = 2$.
When nothing is broken, the limit equals the value of the rule, so substitute $x = 2$.
Multiplying first and then adding, that gives $3(2) + 1 = 6 + 1$.
So the expression approaches the value $7$ as $x \to 2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sneak up with a table
steps: Now from above: x = 2.1 gives 7.3, and x = 2.01 gives 7.03.
Both sides are squeezing toward the same number, 7. That is the limit.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it off the line
steps: y = 3x + 1 is a straight line with no gaps anywhere.
Walk your finger along the line toward x = 2 and watch the height.
The height arrives exactly at 7 — for an unbroken graph, "heading toward" and "lands on" are the same thing.
